companyDescription:
WorkSimplr started with a simple but urgent question:
Why is it so hard for capable students to get real work experience — and why are businesses still struggling to find help?
Jodi McPherson saw this firsthand as a parent and a business leader. Students with talent, grit, and potential were stuck on the sidelines. Traditional internships were gatekept, time-consuming, and often left people out — especially first-gen students, community college learners, and anyone who didn’t have the “right” connections.
So she flipped the model.
WorkSimplr was built to make work accessible: short-term, paid, real-world projects embedded into higher ed systems. No fluff. No false barriers. Just opportunity — for students to earn and learn, and for companies to get work done faster.
It started as a scrappy pilot. Now it’s a movement.
WorkSimplr exists to create pathways that didn’t exist—until now. And it’s doing it with clarity, purpose, and relentless heart.

summary:
Hey, home service business owners, are you tired of trying to get your HVAC, electrical, or plumbing techs to sell? Me, too.
I’m Rodney Koop, president and founder of The New Flat Rate. I’ve been in this industry for more than 40 years and have been a business owner for more than three decades.
For a long time, I thought if I hired clean, sharp, articulate technicians, then I could teach them to sell. Oh, and I certainly tried. I put them through every sales class there was. I tried videos and tapes. I suggested books I love on salesmanship, like Zig Ziglar. I tried to tell them they could make more money, that it would be better for their families, and for our customers.
It never worked. But there is a better way. The home service industry has to start thinking like the retail industry.
Waiters and waitresses don't have to sell, do they? Why is that? It’s because they use a simple pre-printed list — a menu. When a menu is done right, guess what? There's no selling. Menu pricing is so simple that servers do it every single day with no sales resistance, no price objection, and no buyer’s remorse.
So, stop selling. Let the customer buy. Leave the power in the customers’ hands. They will always buy more than you could ever sell them.
When you’re ready, learn how The New Flat Rate menu pricing system can transform your home service contracting business.

headline: CEO & Founder @ Movo | Compliance Infrastructure for Healthcare & Government | Board Member | Fulbright | Ex Uber, McKinsey
companyDescription:
Movo is the location & proof of presence layer for healthcare compliance and government program integrity. We answer "who was where, when, working on what" at the point of care or service delivery, without cameras, spyware, or biometrics, and with zero integrations. Records are identity‑accurate, exception‑aware, provider‑visible, and audit‑ready.

Under the hood, multi‑sensor fusion (NFC phone tap, short‑range radio beacons, zone tags, and event correlation) produces real-time proof of presence and flags phantom visits, GPS spoofing, and credential sharing. Providers see the signals used; documented exceptions are reconciled so reported compliance is defensible. Evidence bundles export cleanly for regulators, auditors, and payers.

Where it's used: Medicaid Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) for home health and personal care; state social services program integrity; government grant verification; 21st Century Cures Act compliance. Near‑term focus: US home health agencies facing Hard Launch enforcement and state programs rebuilding verification infrastructure.

Typical first‑60‑day results: EVV match rates exceed 95%, denied claims drop 30-50%, audit exceptions fall 40-60%.

We also operate Movo Frontline for distributed operations (with real-time task routing and dynamic roster optimization) delivering 10-30% productivity improvements across logistics, healthcare, manufacturing, and hospitality. Used by 700K+ daily users.

People perform at their highest level when they feel appreciated and valued. Obvious, right? But consistently putting that into action—at scale—is where most leaders struggle.

At a golf tournament, we gifted participants a top-of-the-line Callaway driver. It felt like the perfect gift—until people started asking:

↳ “Can I get a fairway wood instead?”
↳ “Do you have a putter or bag?”
↳ “I already own this driver—can I swap it?”

That was the lightbulb moment: even a premium gift falls flat if it’s not personal.
The solution? Choice.

When people can choose a gift they actually want, it creates lasting appreciation—and a lasting impression of the brand behind it.

That insight became the foundation for Cultivate. We’ve supported thousands of client gifting programs, learning what it takes to deliver thoughtful, personal, and scalable appreciation that drives real results.

Today, we help founders and leadership teams turn corporate gifting from a check-the-box gesture into a smart growth strategy. Our approach treats gifting as a business investment—one that improves employee retention, deepens client relationships, and delivers what we call Return on Appreciation™ (ROA).

It’s not about swag. It’s about impact.
I believe in this so much, I got it tattooed on my shoulder. (Really.)

If you’re building a business where people and relationships matter—and want a strategic
